title: Lifting a stably-free complex from a residue quotient
statement: Let $R$ be a ring and $I\subseteq R$ an ideal such that every element of $1+I$ is invertible in $R$. Call a module $M$ over a ring $A$ finite stably free if $M\oplus A^{\oplus m}\cong A^{\oplus n}$ for some integers $m,n\ge0$. Let $K$ be an object of $D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] that is pseudo-coherent [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex], that is, isomorphic in $D(R)$ to a bounded-above complex of finite free $R$-modules. Let $E^\bullet$ be a bounded-above complex of finite stably free $R/I$-modules representing $K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R/I$ in $D(R/I)$. Then $K$ is represented in $D(R)$ by a bounded-above complex $P^\bullet$ of finite stably free $R$-modules such that $P^\bullet\otimes_RR/I$ is isomorphic to $E^\bullet$ as a complex; moreover, $P^i$ is free for every $i$ such that $E^i$ is free.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-complex-lift-class-projective] with $\mathcal P$ the finite stably free $R$-modules. A finite stably free module is finite projective. The class is closed under direct summands and finite direct sums, and the short-exact two-out-of-three property follows because projective short exact sequences split. If a map in the class is surjective modulo $I$, its cokernel is finitely generated and vanishes modulo $I$, so Nakayama's lemma and the hypothesis that every element of $1+I$ is a unit make it zero. Every finite stably free $R/I$-module lifts to a finite stably free $R$-module by lifting a stable presentation $E\oplus(R/I)^m\cong(R/I)^n$ and taking the kernel of the lifted split projection. Finally, pseudo-coherence supplies a bounded-above finite-free representative of $K$, whose terms lie in $\mathcal P$. Thus the general lemma gives a bounded-above complex of finite stably free $R$-modules representing $K$ and reducing termwise to $E^\bullet$. For the final assertion (More on Algebra, Tag 0BC6), let $E^i\cong(R/I)^{\oplus n}$. Since $P^i$ is finite projective with $P^i/IP^i\cong E^i$, lift the resulting surjection $R^{\oplus n}\to(R/I)^{\oplus n}\cong P^i/IP^i$ to a map $\varphi:R^{\oplus n}\to P^i$. It is surjective modulo $I$, hence surjective by Nakayama's lemma (the cokernel is finite and vanishes modulo $I$), hence split as $P^i$ is projective: $R^{\oplus n}\cong P^i\oplus N$ with $N=\operatorname{Ker}\varphi$ finite. Reducing modulo $I$, $(R/I)^{\oplus n}\cong P^i/IP^i\oplus N/IN$ with $\varphi$ modulo $I$ an isomorphism, so $N/IN=0$ and $N=0$ by Nakayama. Hence $P^i\cong R^{\oplus n}$ is free; this holds for every such $i$ simultaneously, with no further choice.
